chapter_title: Concerning the Garment of the Waters: how great is its Measure.
chapter_note: This chapter is wrapped in a strong hagiographic-historical frame (Shapur, Tigris flood, disciples’ praise). The oldest layer appears mainly in the middle as systematic cosmological explanation of the First Man’s elemental garments and the ‘garment of waters’ being drunk by the rulers of death, with sevenfold/measure language. Several teaching units are embedded in dialogue attributions and occasional first-person/citational phrases (e.g., reference to the ‘Great Gospel’), which look like later compilation-layer delivery rather than the impersonal substrate.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure hagiographic-historical apparatus (apostle before King Shapur); no cosmological exposition.
Extended narrative scene-setting about the Tigris flood (time/month/city); functions as story frame, not cosmos→cosmos mapping.
Narrative staging with explicit institutional marker ‘leaders of his church’; compilation frame voice.

paragraphs.core_text: How great is the power of the garment of the waters? How far shall [it extend]? That it should enter with the roar of its flood and fill this river Tigris in its vastness like the mighty sea! It has carried waves from river bank to bank, and run from wall to wall. The source from which all these waters burst forth, how great will it be? For they come and come each year at their appointed season!
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue staging: “One of his disciples then spoke. He says to the apostle:” (compilation frame attribution).
paragraphs.temporal_note: A substantive cosmological question (“garment of the waters”, measure/extent/source) embedded in a dialogue frame; the question itself is the teaching prompt.
Dialogue delivery and exhortation (‘listen to what I am about to tell you’) rather than impersonal cosmological exposition; functions as transition within the frame.

paragraphs.core_text: [At] the time when the First Man assumed the elements, and stood [fi]rm against the first enmity that had come about in the darkness, he defied these great and powerful rulers. They are immeasurable, greater than the extent or size of thousands and ten thousands of parasangs. At the start, when he spread the fight against them, he gave them fire and wind; and afterwards he gave the garment of the waters to the rulers of death. So they, the rulers, drank in and consumed those waters. Many [waters] poured forth from the garment of waters [...] the rivers flow. The mouth of the rulers [...] those [...], the warriors of destruction [...] laboured and brought them forth.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed first-person/citational clause anchoring to Mani’s book tradition: “the way that I told] you in the Great Gospel.”
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core cosmological mechanism (First Man assumes elements; garments used as weapons; rulers of death drinking waters) with a later referential seam to an authored ‘Great Gospel’ and first-person address.

paragraphs.core_text: There were seven (rivers), like the great river Tigris [that you] see, flowing in to the mouth of each one of them, as they shall not [...] to a single stomach, to their fill; because in turn the descent to its stomach shall burn them with its fire and heat. Those rulers were like the [...] of [...]; they were not emptied; rain and [...] their existent days.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic sevenfold cosmological description (rivers → mouths/stomachs of rulers; internal mechanics of burning/heat). Despite the simile, the mapping remains within the mythic system.

paragraphs.core_text: The measure of that river was expanded seven times, as they flow [...] of the body of the [...] waters [...] now.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue attribution (“The apostle speaks to that elect one:”) and removed extended exhortation/marveling rhetoric that follows the cosmological measure statement.
paragraphs.temporal_note: A compact, structural ‘measure expanded seven times’ teaching embedded in explicit dialogue attribution and followed by exhortative amplification (later delivery layer).

paragraphs.core_text: [...] is how great a struggle, since it has [...] these creatures of destruction, the mighty giants. Behold, they are entwined, bound, and [...] in every place. They are hidden, not revealed before the eyes of every flesh that exists on the land of death [...]. These rulers [...] revealed. The entire universe of flesh will be destroyed and dissolved [...]; all pass away [...]. They will be destroyed with their angry voice, which is mightier than the thunder.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic process/eschatology (binding/hidden rulers; dissolution of the universe of flesh) without institutional targeting; retains mythic-mechanical voice.

Rhetorical comparison anchored to the specific earthly Tigris and first-person delivery (‘of which I have recounted to you’); functions as narrative application within the scene rather than substrate exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: ... the measure of the elements of the waters. ... the stature of the Man who bore them. ... how great is that god, active in power, the one whom these waters [...] than the stature of the First Man who [assumed] this garment of such size; and how much was made.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed imperative/exhortative scaffolding (“See [...] and be amazed... Marvel... And understand...”) to retain the underlying cosmological valuation of measure/stature/power.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Underlying cosmological valuation (measure of elements; stature of First Man) is old-style content, but it is delivered through direct exhortation typical of later pedagogical framing.
Closing reverence/thanks formula addressed to ‘our master’; classic hagiographic frame closure.
